note: China, read in the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau Exit-Entry Administration's service guide for issuing, changing and extending a foreigner's residence permit for work (the Beijing government service portal, PDF dated 26 March 2026), resting on the Exit and Entry Administration Law and the Regulations on the Administration of Foreigners' Entry and Exit. A foreigner who comes to work (a performer on the Z visa, with the culture or sports authority's performance licence, letters and name list) asks the exit-entry office for a work-type residence permit within China; it is decided in 5 working days for holders of a category A work permit notice and 7 for others, and is valid from 90 days to 5 years, so no single term is kept. It is tied to the employer that applies (the work permit notice and the unit's letter), read as work for the sponsor. Its fee is not stated in the guide and was not found in a published national schedule (a web search found only the 2004 Ministry of Finance reply allowing a fee to be set later); none is kept. Permanent residence (the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card) and naturalisation were not read: the National Immigration Administration's site (www.nia.gov.cn) and the NPC's law database did not answer this client. The guide is Beijing's; other provinces' offices apply the same national law.
